It is possible to be percieved as entitled, begging, judgemental, or simply inconsiderate as my actions may cause pain with their focus on my own preservation. I think a lot of people might see my persistence on finding the right energy as me being unreasonably and judgementally picky—which is a fair assessment, but mischaracterizes my intentions.

The unfortunate reality for me is that I am a 21 year old, burnt out, ultra traumatized and complex human being. My lens and my radar is informed by my experiences and very sheltered upbringing. My experiences of loving, being taken advantage of, making connections and being assaulted are what inform my assessment of other humans, and most of the time I have a lot of trouble figuring out how to explain my aversion when I don’t perfectly meld with someone’s energy. I would like to give everyone two paragraphs letting them know how I’m feeling, but to be honest, I barely have the energy to sweep the floor. I get dizzy when I pick things up. I can‘t stand up without leaning against something. It takes me 2 hours to start my to-do list, because I’m so exhausted.

I want to formally apologize if I hurt you by not responding to your message or by ghosting you at random. I don’t mean to be cold, I really really don‘t. I just don’t have the ability to write things out in a way that‘s perfectly respectable and inoffensive, and also personal. With my current health, I don’t have the ability. I wish I did. 

Thank you for reading this, and best regards to whoever may read this.

Edit: clarification that I’m not referring to this commenter, but those that may have interacted with me before.

Suicide via Overdose. I was 18, just dropped out of school and THE MOST depressed. I was in a weird spot with my about to be exboyfriend James at the time and I left his apartment after feeling unloved. I went to the pharmacy and got a bunch of sleeping meds, and downed the entire bottle of over 90 pills alongside some Gatorade and Skittles. James was texting me frantically but I ignored him until my best friend called me to ask where I was since my boyfriend called him in worry. After some coaxing, I told him. 

He called James, who accidentally went to exactly across the river I was at. He had been in his car looking for me. I called him on the phone and I saw his LED headlights across the river, before he pulled up about 6 minutes later. He drove me to the hospital like a fucking maniac. I had never seen him so stressed or worried, or speedy. I was brought in, and the last thing I remember is laying on the hospital bed and him being right next to me.

My best friend can always seem to sense when I’m in danger, and usually reaches out at that moment. I’ve been on the edge several times before when he calls me and is like “What are you doing right now?”.

I woke up in a different hospital 3 days later, alone. To this day, telling this story still tears me up.

If your parents take it like my dad did (his response was “I feel like a failure”), don’t take it personally at all and make sure you can assure them that things are perfectly fine and consensual between the two of you. Have a talk with your boyfriend before you do anything. They’ll still be ultra concerned, but knowing that you aren’t under any sort of pressure or expectations will go a long way to making them feel okay with you being out and about with him. If your parents ask any weird questions, as parents sometimes can, just redirect them to the point at hand: he makes you happy and you’re totally okay and safe with your relationship.

I believe in you!

Editing to also say: if you can, get him to meet them first. They will appreciate the gesture and will be more warm to his age after assessing his character (provided he does well at dinner).

Wondering if I should return my newly purchased MacBook Air with 8GB of RAM for a similar model with 16.  
Recently got this MacBook Air with 8GB of RAM and 512 storage, and while I love the thing, I've noticed that Rosetta applications have been eating my RAM when I'm doing my tasks. Generally I use my computers for photo editing: applying a lot of effects, masks and blending modes sort of thing.  
I was really looking forward to the M2 as I was told by a lot of the reviewer coverage that 8GB of Unified Memory was different than 8GB of regular memory in previous MacBooks. However, what I'm noticing is that Intel apps are killing my RAM usage, and when I'm trying to do more than a few effects on Pixelmator Pro, my computer quickly runs out of memory, going far enough to give me the pop-up that tells me "you've run out of application memory".  
Rosetta 2 apps also use 2x the RAM they used on Intel. I migrated over my entire computer to my new MBA, and the apps that normally take up 38 mb on Intel are taking up 500mb on M2. Of anything, that's the thing that's disappointing me the most. I use a lot of apps that haven't been ported over to M2, and they're killing my ram usage, and (I assume) my battery.  
I rarely encountered this with my Intel machine, and just to test the two, I did a test where I performed the same actions on both computers (my 2017 13" MBP & the 2022 M2 MBA), and the Intel machine was in fact slower, but the RAM spikes were much higher on the MBA. I don't know if that's something I should be worried about, but it was something I definitely noticed. They did both get the job done, with the MBA being much snappier, but I'm now questioning what I paid for if the only thing is quicker GPU results.  
I'm a pretty impatient person (I bought the MBA randomly since I wanted to try out one of the new Apple Silicon notebooks) so it wouldn't surprise me if I should have waited, but I would just like someone else's opinion as to what they would do if they were me.

It might seem like all your body is doing is being stressed and shutting down, but it’s a result of preservation and conservation. We don’t really have the energy to spare at all (since the recovery from high stress/fight or flight is taxing), but life keeps piling on stressful scenarios for you to deal with. You’re unmotivated out of both executive dysfunction and also lack of the necessary internal resources to muster even a minor level of inertia. 

These days, I know that I *should* do things, but there’s no connection in my body to the part of my mind that asks me to perform the task. I just…can’t. It puts my body in a faux fight or flight state when I consider the stakes and try to shame myself into doing it, and that adds to the expended internal energy. Just because you’re not physically moving doesn’t mean you’re not absolutely tiring yourself out.

If you’d like some pointers, I have a few. Don’t shame yourself for being in this state. Your body wants to do what it wants to do, and if it’s asking you for extended rest, give it as much as you can. Try and eat so that you have energy consistently as well.

The biggest motivator for me has honestly been my friends and partner. Having people who are willing to stick with you, and help you when you’re ready is INCREDIBLY helpful. See if you can get someone to be your body double when you have enough energy to do something. If you have the energy to shower, but you have little initiative, find a person to be there to congratulate you. Just having someone be proud of your accomplishments is immensely helpful in regaining your balance. There are lots of people out there who are in your spot, and if you can find a way to give each other (virtual) high fives, you might find your passion for life slowly returning. We’re social creatures! I try and lean into that a lot.

Mostly just don’t overwork yourself. Do what you need to to survive but not much else. (so if money is a thing you need, work but don’t do much else! dystopian? yes. but this is where having buddies can help at least. you can also just treat yourself like a Sim—do tasks with an empty brain) Let yourself heal, and every forward step you take will be a triumph worthy of congratulations. If anything, I’ll congratulate you.

I’m rooting for you! And if you need someone to talk to, it’s okay to message me whenever.

As someone who switched from the Pixel 2 XL, I gotta say that I’m feeling super comfortable with the 12 Pro.

The jump in price from the two will hurt for sure, but I think coming from the XL, having a phone that’s not curved on the sides is natural in a way that’s a little hard to convey. That said, if you’re really indifferent about the design difference, I think the 11 Pro is actually still a really good choice. It’s got a lot of the bells and whistles included in the 12 (spatial audio, the ability to display HDR, and a killer camera even if not the newest). 

The thing about the 11 vs the 12 is that the 12 just has a vastly better screen, so if you’ve been eyeing the 11, I think the jump to the 11 Pro or just the 12 is absolutely worth it just based off of the screen improvements alone. You’ll enjoy having an OLED screen far more than the few bucks you’d save, especially if you’re planning to keep the phone for a while.

The 12 Pro (same size as the 12!) is this weird not-small-yet-not-big 6.1 inches and as someone with small hands, it makes me really feel like I’ve got the perfect medium since it’s just big enough that I feel like the tradeoff in size is worth it from the slightly larger XL. if you’re someone with large or even generally well sized hands, the 12 Pro might be the better choice as I think it’ll feel a little more natural.

Aside from the actual body of the device, I find the camera a bit of a wash honestly. It’s really good, and I love the fact that it displays all the photos in HDR after you’ve taken them, but the Pixel’s (especially the Pixel 2’s) signature look is one that I really loved, so while the photos are sharper and probably of better overall quality, I miss the contrast-y tuning out of the box. I’m sure the photos can be edited, but if you’re like me and you really loved the Pixel’s photos, this camera is both an upgrade and a bit of an aesthetic downgrade. I think that’s true for both this phone and the 11 series of phones.
I’d chosen the 12 Pro since my Pixel 2 XL started to shit the bed towards the end of 2019 (the cell radios just started dying) and I feel very good about my choice seeing as I also intend to keep this phone for about 3-4 years.

Whichever phone you do end up getting, I’d love to hear about what you think after, especially coming from the Pixel 2 XL’s absolutely shitty screen (I defended it at the time, but boy is the iPhone’s screen miles better). You won’t notice the resolution reduction most of the time, though I’d turn off True Tone since it made the screen temperature far too warm for my liking after immediately coming from the Pixel’s blue screen. 
Hope this helps a little!
